scope: Independent mathematical/source review, separate integer/factorial checks, inspection of recorded build and native evidence, and one native PNG. No local Lean replay or formal implementation verification.

checks.detail: Inspected the prime inverse-pair proof and composite-prime-divisor converse. For n >= 2, the least nonnegative residue is zero exactly at prime inputs; integer division returns the correct indicator.
0 and 1 are separately classified as neither. The proof that every composite n > 4 has residue 1 is valid; n = 4 has residue 3. Prime-square endpoints are included.
Inspected both candidate functions in Python and C#. Neither receives a sieve, earlier labels or a prime list. Sieve data appear only inside verification routines.

Python uses integer modulo/division; native Wilson uses long intermediate products within its 100000 cap. Native trial uses divisor <= n/divisor, avoiding square overflow. Zero-product early exit preserves the final factorial residue.

Independently evaluated all 2001 integers 0..2000 using every proper divisor and direct math.factorial(n-1), and matched trial, Wilson and both f() dispatches. Counts: 303 primes, 1696 composites, 2 neither.
Independently rejected 13 invalid calls covering negatives, bools, float, string, None and an unknown evaluation method. Worked 96/97 operation counts and phases match exact arithmetic.

Verified hashes and inspected the recorded Python sieve check through 100000, full-factorial/Wilson check through 2000, special controls and bounded five-run timing. These recorded broader checks were not independently rerun by this reviewer.

Inspected the new command branch, candidate parsing, trial/Wilson methods, native built-in verification and export schema. Candidate 96 is accepted directly rather than through the prefiltered prime dropdown.

Independently checked 696 emitted records across six exports using integer factors, full factorial residues where available, domain limits and phases. Controls select 0, 4, 96, 97, 100001, 2147483647; the two above-cap candidates retain exact trial results with unavailable Wilson fields.

Read the successful Release build log and bound the executable, DLL, project and runtime configuration. Final native reports record DOTNET_ROLL_FORWARD=Major. Earlier lock/launch recovery is producer-recorded and was not replayed during review.
Independently sampled all 101 indexed tile interiors in the 1920x1080 PNG: 25 violet primes, 74 composite fills and 2 neither. This is an indexed fill check, not OCR.

Viewed the main selected 97 PNG at full resolution. Formula, 96/97 results, n = 4 exception,all 0..100 labels, legend and scope footers are legible without material clipping. The true 3.75-degree and 0-degree phasors are intentionally close. Control images were not visually reviewed.
Phase is computed only for illustration after exact residue classification. The proof explains same-quadrant aliasing and why tolerance or pixel resolution must not decide primality.

Verified Gamma factorial/holomorphy sources and the argument for H(n)=0 iff prime on integers n >= 2. H(1)=0 and intermediate-value zeros in (4, 5) are correctly identified; the extension is not the implemented decision rule or an RH claim.

Operation-count and bit-length caveats are accurate. Trial and Wilson are established methods; timings are explicitly bounded observations. Counting inversion still requires work and no direct fast nth-prime algorithm or speed breakthrough is claimed.

README accurately distinguishes native Int32/Wilson-cap scope from Python arbitrary-precision integer inputs, documents runtime roll-forward and separates standard-library arithmetic checks from native rendering QA. All bound report inputs and current review inputs exist and match hashes.

independentPython.oracle: Every proper divisor and direct math.factorial(n-1)

independentNative.oracle: Exact potential divisors through isqrt(n), plus full factorial residues where Wilson is available

limits: The mathematical all-n theorem is distinct from finite implementation coverage.
The broader native sieve tests are observed through the hash-bound exported verification reports, not a separate reviewer run of 100001 native calls.
Only the main selected 97 PNG was visually inspected; controls were checked as JSON.
No formal proof-assistant replay, new theorem, speedup, prime-prediction breakthrough or RH result is established.
